detail.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

## What does this PR do?

Install cuBLAS 13.8.1 (package version `13.8.1.7`) in the dev CI image to pick up the fix for:
A standalone CUDA C++ reproducer on two GB200 GPUs shows cublasLtMatmul intermittently leaving output elements unchanged during concurrent NCCL communication, despite beta=0. One process uses one host thread per GPU, with no PyTorch or Transformer Engine dependency. Routing to cuBLASLt for investigation; attribution among cuBLAS, NCCL, the driver, and hardware remains unresolved.

The Docker build selects the official CUDA 13 archive for x86_64 or Arm SBSA and replaces the toolkit's cuBLAS/cuBLASLt libraries and headers before compiling native dependencies. Installing into the existing toolkit paths ensures PyTorch uses the updated libraries. `CUBLAS_VERSION` is a build argument.

Sources: [13.8.1 download archive](https://developer.nvidia.com/cublas-13-8-1-download-archive), [version metadata](https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cublas/redist/redistrib_13.8.1.json).

## Validation

- Dockerfile build checks passed against the cached NGC PyTorch 26.06 image.
- Built the added installation layer on Arm64 with NGC PyTorch 26.06. Both cuBLAS and cuBLASLt report 13.8.1, headers report 13.8.1.7, and the PyTorch process maps both updated `.so.13.8.1.7` files.
- Built the same installation layer on x86_64 with Ubuntu 24.04. Both runtime libraries report 13.8.1, headers report 13.8.1.7, and the unversioned/SONAME symlinks resolve to the updated files.
- Shell syntax, `git diff --check`, and `CHECK_ONLY=true bash tools/autoformat.sh` passed; no Python files changed.

The initial local PyTorch loading check used cached NGC PyTorch 26.06 because resolving the then-configured 26.08 image returned an authorization error. After rebasing onto main, Dockerfile build checks also passed against NGC PyTorch 26.09. Earlier [GPU CI run `36493748270`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/36493748270) predates checksum removal and the rebase onto PyTorch 26.09. A full dev image build and GPU validation have not been rerun locally for the current revision.

detail.title: build: install cuBLAS 13.8.1 in the dev CI image

files.patch:
@@ -88,6 +88,32 @@ RUN --mount=type=bind,source=docker/common/install_nccl.sh,target=/opt/install_n
     esac
 EOF
 
+ARG CUBLAS_VERSION=13.8.1.7
+RUN bash -euxo pipefail <<"EOF"
+    # cuBLAS 13.8.1 includes the grouped GEMM correctness fix.
+    case "${TARGETARCH}" in
+        amd64)
+            CUBLAS_ARCH=x86_64
+            ;;
+        arm64)
+            CUBLAS_ARCH=sbsa
+            ;;
+        *) echo "Unsupported TARGETARCH for cuBLAS: ${TARGETARCH}" >&2; exit 1 ;;
+    esac
+    CUBLAS_ARCHIVE="libcublas-linux-${CUBLAS_ARCH}-${CUBLAS_VERSION}_cuda13-archive"
+    CUBLAS_TMP=$(mktemp -d)
+    curl -fLSs --retry 3 -o "${CUBLAS_TMP}/cublas.tar.xz" \
+        "https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cublas/redist/libcublas/linux-${CUBLAS_ARCH}/${CUBLAS_ARCHIVE}.tar.xz"
+    tar -xJf "${CUBLAS_TMP}/cublas.tar.xz" -C "${CUBLAS_TMP}"
+    # Replace the toolkit copies so existing linker paths pick up both cuBLAS and cuBLASLt.
+    CUDA_ROOT="${CUDA_HOME:-/usr/local/cuda}"
+    cp -a "${CUBLAS_TMP}/${CUBLAS_ARCHIVE}/include/." "${CUDA_ROOT}/include/"
+    cp -a "${CUBLAS_TMP}/${CUBLAS_ARCHIVE}/lib/." "${CUDA_ROOT}/lib64/"
+    install -Dm644 "${CUBLAS_TMP}/${CUBLAS_ARCHIVE}/LICENSE" "${CUDA_ROOT}/doc/cublas/LICENSE"
+    ldconfig
+    rm -rf "${CUBLAS_TMP}"
+EOF
+
 COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock /workspace/
 COPY docker/patches/mamba-cxx20.patch /workspace/mamba-cxx20.patch
 COPY megatron/core/__init__.py /workspace/megatron/core/

inline_comments.body: This looks fishy. The iteration time goes up in the middle of the training and then never goes down to the same level? Is it reproducible?
this looks like an issue with the first run. 2 runs later doesn't seem to have this issue.

same issue on the rerun
```
Training attempt | Step 26 | Step 27 | Average, steps 28–50
-- | -- | -- | --
1 | 0.396 s | 5.998 s | 3.379 s
2 | 0.403 s | 0.427 s | 0.404 s
3 | 0.410 s | 0.437 s | 0.411 s
```

I reran this on EOS (`6142633`, 8× H100), with a detailed comparison against the failing CI run.

To verify configuration parity, I:

- Checked out CI’s exact merge commit, `0e9bc555`.
- Rebuilt from CI’s **pinned NGC base-image digest**, using the same Dockerfile, dependency lockfile, and native build arguments.
- Verified the loaded runtime libraries: PyTorch `2.14.0a0+4fdf77b940.nv26.08`, TE `5e52befd`, cuBLAS `13.8.1.7`, and NCCL `2.30.7`.
- Used the original `run_ci_test.sh` / `ft_launcher` path, with the same model configuration, paths, and NCCL defaults. Started from a clean environment to exclude inherited EOS settings.
- Compared **all 887 printed training arguments: zero differences**.
- Compared every step’s loss, gradient norm, zero count, parameter norm, and both checked memory metrics: **all 50 values were bit-identical to CI in all three attempts**.

Each attempt used a fresh container. The first started with zero resident dataset pages.

| Attempt | CI average, steps 28–50 | EOS average, steps 28–50 |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 3.379 s | 0.357 s |
| 2 | 0.404 s | 0.354 s |
| 3 | 0.411 s | 0.347 s |

So the computation and configuration now match, but the timing cliff still does not reproduce. Remaining differences include the host driver (`580.82.07` in CI versus `535.129.03` on EOS), storage, and Docker versus Pyxis/Enroot. The image was rebuilt from CI’s inputs, rather than pulled from the original ECR artifact.

The cause remains unverified; the next useful measurement is per-phase timing on the CI runner itself.
